title: Liquid Glass — An idea becomes a connected system

scenes.title: Droplet of an idea
scenes.purpose: A single liquid-glass droplet forms over a striped board while the headline arrives on the dark field.
visuals: Three.js MeshPhysicalMaterial transmission droplet refracting navy/off-white stripes and an accent band
Displaced-sphere liquid wobble driven by timeline time
Headline copy fading up line by line on the dark left field

beats.development: A small glass droplet appears (back.out) and the kicker LENS / CONNECTION fades in.
The droplet swells into a large lens and glides left; the stripes behind it bend into curved bands. Headline lines stagger in.

scenes.title: Strands branch out
scenes.purpose: The idea splits into four connected glass nodes.
visuals: Four accent-coloured tubes draw out from inside the lens along curved paths
Glass node droplets ride the strand tips, stretching then settling
Panel edges and stripes refract through each node

beats.development: Staggered strands carry nodes to four positions; the hub's wobble begins to calm.

scenes.title: Connected system holds
scenes.purpose: The network settles and lights once, then holds for reading.
visuals: Hub wobble reaches zero by 2.45 s; full frame static from about 2.6 s

beats.development: Link glow pulse, then a still hold of the complete composition and headline.
captions: An idea becomes a connected system.

findings: One primary focus per beat: droplet, then branching strands, then the settled system.
Headline fully legible from 1.11 s, nearly 1.9 s of exposure.
All motion settled by about 2.6 s.
justifiedHolds: 2.5–3.0 s still hold so the finished system and copy can be read.

notes: Silent preview; no audio track was produced.
Blender was not used by explicit user instruction; Three.js physical transmission replaces it.
Background chosen per scene_dependent policy: a deep ink field with a graphic striped board, so the refraction is easy to see. This replaces the earlier warm canvas.
